# Lavendar Lewis

## Overview

- **Age:** Forty-five years old  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c23 P9](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0009)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c1 P46](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0046), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v2 c30 P30](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0030)</sub>
- **Origin:** Grafton  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Miss Lavendar  <sub>[v2 c21 P39](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0039), [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045)</sub>

## Appearance

Miss Lavendar is a small, slim lady with snow-white wavy hair arranged in puffs and coils. Beneath her white tresses she possesses a fresh, girlish, pink-cheeked face with soft wood-brown eyes that have golden glints, a sweet-lipped mouth, and dimples. She has a musical voice reminiscent of white satin and tinkling water, and she delights in wearing frilly, dainty gowns of pale-hued muslin.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002), [v2 c23 P5](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0005), [v2 c23 P9](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0009)_

## Personality

Miss Lavendar is an imaginative, romantic, and youthful woman who imaginative-lays out fairy-like amusements to keep her life bright. Though warm, sweet, and hospitable to young people, she admits to being sulky and proud when her feelings or tempers are crossed. She possesses an imaginative spirit akin to Anne Shirley's, frequently populating her lonely home with imaginary guests and a dream-child.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c21 P56](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0056), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019), [v2 c27 P59](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0059)_

## Traits

- Imaginative and romantic  <sub>[v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c21 P56](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0056)</sub>
- Proud and sulky  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>

- Rebellious against growing old  <sub>[v2 c23 P9](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0009)</sub>

## Abilities

- Cooking and baking delicacies  <sub>[v2 c21 P53](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0053), [v2 c27 P29](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0029)</sub>

## Goals

- To keep the freshness of youth and romance in her life  <sub>[v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c23 P9](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0009)</sub>

## History

Miss Lavendar Lewis lived a secluded life in a secluded stone house called Echo Lodge in Middle Grafton, kept company by a series of young handmaidens whom she called 'Charlotta'. Twenty-five years prior, she had been engaged to Stephen Irving, but a silly quarrel and her own proud sulkiness parted them, leading Stephen to leave for the United States. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry stumbled upon her hidden home while lost and immediately befriended her, enjoying her imaginative hospitality. Later, Anne brought Stephen's son, Paul Irving, to visit Miss Lavendar, which eventually led to Stephen Irving returning to see her. The two reconciled their old misunderstanding, renewed their engagement, and were married in the garden under the honeysuckle trellis before departing for a new life together in Boston.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c21 P49](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0049), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c23 P15](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0015), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019), [v2 c23 P29](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0029), [v2 c28 P35](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0035), [v2 c28 P42](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0042), [v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029), [v2 c30 P33](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0033)_

## Background by volume

- Daughter of a father who named her Lavendar after the scent of his wife's home  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- Engaged twenty-five years earlier to Stephen Irving before a foolish quarrel broke it off  <sub>[v2 c23 P15](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0015), [v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>
- Lived for years in a secluded stone house called Echo Lodge with young hired girls named Charlotta  <sub>[v2 c21 P28](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0028), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Quotes

> A person must have some compensations. I don't believe I could live at times if I didn't pretend things.  <sub>[v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054)</sub>

> Some are born old maids, some achieve old maidenhood, and some have old maidenhood thrust upon them.  <sub>[v2 c23 P13](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0013)</sub>

> Pride and sulkiness make a very bad combination, Anne.  <sub>[v2 c23 P19](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0019)</sub>
